sentences.zh: 何復，字見元，平度人。

translations.literal: He Fu, styled Jianyuan, was a native of Pingdu.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu, whose style name was Jianyuan, came from Pingdu.

sentences.zh: 邵宗元，字景康，碭山人。

translations.literal: Shao Zongyuan, styled Jingkang, was a native of Dangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zongyuan, styled Jingkang, was from Dangshan.

sentences.zh: 復，崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: Fu passed the metropolitan examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu earned his jinshi degree in the seventh year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 知高縣，有卻賊功。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Gao County he had merit in repelling bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Gao County he distinguished himself by driving off bandits.

sentences.zh: 忤上官，被劾謫戍。

translations.literal: He offended his superiors and was impeached and banished to frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: After he crossed his superiors, they impeached him and sent him to frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 後廷臣多論薦，起英山知縣，累遷工部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: Later many court officials recommended him; he was raised to magistrate of Yingshan, then promoted through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Works and advanced to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Later many officials at court spoke up for him; he was recalled as magistrate of Yingshan and rose step by step to director and then vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月擢保定知府。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was promoted to prefect of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen he was appointed prefect of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 宗元，由恩貢生歷保定同知，有治行。

translations.literal: Zongyuan, through the en gong route, served as vice prefect of Baoding and had a record of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan had entered service as an en gong graduate, served as vice prefect of Baoding, and was known for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷山西，遣偽副將軍劉方亮由固關東犯，畿輔震動。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng seized Shanxi and sent the false deputy general Liu Fangliang to invade eastward through Guyuan Pass; the capital region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng overran Shanxi, he sent his so-called deputy general Liu Fangliang east through Guyuan Pass, and the metropolitan region trembled.

sentences.zh: 及真定遊擊謝嘉福殺巡撫徐標反，遣使迎賊，人情益洶洶。

translations.literal: When the roving-bandit commander Xie Jiafu at Zhending killed Surintendant Xu Biao and rebelled, sending envoys to welcome the rebels, popular alarm grew ever more acute.
translations.idiomatic: Then at Zhending the guerrilla commander Xie Jiafu killed the provincial commissioner Xu Biao and rose in revolt, dispatching envoys to welcome the rebels, and public panic only deepened.

sentences.zh: 宗元時攝府事，亟集通判王宗周，推官許曰可，清苑知縣朱永康，後衛指揮劉忠嗣及鄉官張羅彥、尹洗等，議城守。

translations.literal: Zongyuan was then acting prefect and hastily gathered Vice Magistrate Wang Zongzhou, Assistant Magistrate Xu Yueke, Qingyuan County Magistrate Zhu Yongkang, Rear Garrison Commander Liu Zhongsi, and local gentry Zhang Luoyan, Yin Xi, and others to discuss defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan was then acting prefect; he quickly assembled Vice Magistrate Wang Zongzhou, Assistant Magistrate Xu Yueke, Qingyuan magistrate Zhu Yongkang, Rear Garrison Commander Liu Zhongsi, and local leaders Zhang Luoyan, Yin Xi, and others to plan the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 復聞，兼程馳入城，宗元授以印。

translations.literal: When Fu heard, he traveled day and night to enter the city; Zongyuan handed him the seal.
translations.idiomatic: Fu heard the news and raced into the city without rest; Zongyuan handed him the official seal.

sentences.zh: 復曰：「公部署已定，印仍佩之，我相與僇力可也。」

translations.literal: Fu said: "Your deployments are already settled—keep wearing the seal. We can strive together with all our might.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Your arrangements are already set—keep the seal. Let us exert ourselves together.

sentences.zh: 乃謁文廟，與諸生講《見危致命章》，詞氣激烈。

translations.literal: Then they visited the Temple of Culture and expounded the chapter on seeing peril and giving one's life to the students, their words fiercely impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: They then went to the Temple of Culture and lectured the students on the chapter "Seeing Danger and Giving One's Life," their words burning with fervor.

sentences.zh: 講畢，登城分守。

translations.literal: When the lecture ended, they ascended the wall and divided the defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture was over, they climbed the walls and divided up the defense.

sentences.zh: 都城陷之次日，賊使投書誘降，宗元手裂之。

translations.literal: The day after the capital fell, rebel envoys delivered a letter to induce surrender; Zongyuan tore it apart with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: On the day after the capital fell, rebel messengers brought a letter urging surrender; Zongyuan tore it to pieces with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊大至，絡繹三百里。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels arrived in force, their columns stretching three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels arrived in full strength, their columns filling the roads for three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 有數十騎服婦人衣，言：「所過百余城，皆開門遠迎，不降即屠。

translations.literal: Several dozen horsemen dressed in women's clothing declared: "Of more than a hundred cities we have passed, all opened their gates from afar to welcome us—refuse to submit and we slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen riders in women's dress called out, "Of the more than a hundred cities we have passed, every one opened its gates from afar to welcome us—refuse to surrender and we slaughter you.

sentences.zh: 且京師已破，汝為誰守？」

translations.literal: Moreover the capital has already fallen—whom are you holding the city for?
translations.idiomatic: The capital is already lost—whom are you defending this city for?

sentences.zh: 城上人聞之，發豎眥裂。

translations.literal: When those atop the walls heard this, they bristled with rage, eyes wide and brows split.
translations.idiomatic: Those on the walls heard this and bristled with rage, eyes blazing and brows knit in fury.

sentences.zh: 賊環攻累日，宗元等守甚堅，賊稍稍引卻。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged for many days; Zongyuan and the others defended very stubbornly, and the rebels gradually drew back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels ringed the city and attacked for days, yet Zongyuan and the others held firm, and the enemy slowly drew off.

sentences.zh: 督師大學士李建泰率殘卒數百，輦餉銀十余輛，叩城求入。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Jiantai, serving as supreme commander, led several hundred shattered troops and carted more than a dozen loads of silver provisions, knocking at the gate to be let in.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Jiantai, serving as supreme commander, brought several hundred broken troops and more than a dozen cartloads of silver provisions, and knocked at the gate asking to be admitted.

sentences.zh: 宗元等不許。

translations.literal: Zongyuan and the others would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan and the others refused.

sentences.zh: 建泰舉敕印示之，宗元等曰：「荷天子厚恩，禦門賜劍，酌酒餞別。

translations.literal: Jiantai displayed the imperial patent and seal; Zongyuan and the others said: "We have received the Son of Heaven's great grace—the emperor himself at the palace gates bestowed the sword and offered wine at our parting.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai held up the imperial patent and seal; Zongyuan and the others said, "We owe the Son of Heaven a great debt of grace—the emperor himself came to the palace gate to bestow the sword and poured wine to send us off.

sentences.zh: 今不仗鉞西征，乃叩關避賊耶？」

translations.literal: Now instead of taking the baton to march west against the enemy, you come knocking at the pass to flee from the rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Now, instead of taking the command baton and marching west against the enemy, you come knocking at the pass to flee from the rebels?

sentences.zh: 建泰怒，厲聲叱呼，且舉尚方劍脅之。

translations.literal: Jiantai raged, shouting harshly, and even raised the imperial sword to threaten them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai flew into a rage, shouting at them in a harsh voice, and even raised the imperial sword to threaten them.

sentences.zh: 或請啟門，宗元曰：「脫賊詐為之，若何？」

translations.literal: Some urged opening the gate; Zongyuan said: "Suppose the rebels are disguising themselves as this—what then?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged opening the gate; Zongyuan said, "What if the rebels are impersonating him—then what?

sentences.zh: 眾以御史金毓峒嘗監建泰軍，識建泰，推出視之信，乃納之。

translations.literal: The crowd noted that Censor Jin Yutong had once supervised Jiantai's army and knew him; they pushed Jin forward to verify, and finding it true, only then admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: The others said that Censor Jin Yutong had once overseen Jiantai's army and knew him; they pushed Jin forward to look, found it was indeed he, and only then let them in.

sentences.zh: 建泰入，賊攻益厲。

translations.literal: After Jiantai entered, rebel attacks grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiantai was inside, the rebel assaults grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 建泰倡言曰：「勢不支矣，姑與議降。」

translations.literal: Jiantai proclaimed: "The situation cannot be held—we might as well discuss surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai began to say openly, "We cannot hold out—let us at least talk of surrender.

sentences.zh: 書牒，迫宗元用印。

translations.literal: He wrote a dispatch and pressed Zongyuan to affix the seal.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted a document and pressed Zongyuan to affix the seal.

sentences.zh: 宗元抵印厲聲曰：「我為朝廷守土，義不降，欲降者任為之。」

translations.literal: Zongyuan pushed back the seal and said sternly: "I hold this soil for the court and will not surrender in duty; whoever wishes to surrender may do as he pleases.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan pushed the seal away and said in a stern voice, "I hold this territory for the court and in duty will not surrender; whoever wishes to submit may do as he likes.

sentences.zh: 大哭，引刀將自刎，左右急止之，皆雨泣。

translations.literal: Weeping loudly, he drew a knife to kill himself; attendants urgently stopped him, and all wept like rain.
translations.idiomatic: He wept aloud, drew a knife to kill himself, and his attendants rushed to stop him while everyone wept as if in a downpour.

sentences.zh: 羅彥前曰：「邪說勿聽，速擊賊。」

translations.literal: Luoyan stepped forward and said: "Pay no heed to wicked talk—strike the rebels at once.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan stepped forward and said, "Do not listen to such wicked talk—strike the rebels at once.

sentences.zh: 復自起巘西洋巨炮，火發，被燎幾死。

translations.literal: Fu himself mounted the great Western cannon on the parapet; when it fired, he was scorched and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu himself manned the great Western cannon on the parapet; when it fired, the blaze scorched him and he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 賊攻無遺力，雉堞盡傾。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked with undiminished force until the battlements were utterly overturned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked with undiminished force until the battlements were utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 俄賊火箭中城西北樓，復遂焚死。

translations.literal: Shortly rebel fire-arrows struck the northwest tower of the city wall and Fu was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a rebel fire-arrow struck the northwest tower, and Fu was burned to death.

sentences.zh: 南郭門又焚，守者多散。

translations.literal: The southern outer gate also burned, and most defenders scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The southern outer gate also caught fire, and most of the defenders scattered.

sentences.zh: 南城守將王登洲縋城出降，賊蜂擁而上。

translations.literal: The southern-wall garrison commander Wang Dengzhou was lowered by rope to surrender; rebels swarmed up.
translations.idiomatic: The southern-wall commander Wang Dengzhou was let down by rope to surrender, and the rebels swarmed up the wall.

sentences.zh: 建泰中軍副將郭中傑等為內應，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Jiantai's central-army deputy Guo Zhongjie and others acted as inside collaborators, and the city was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai's central-army deputy Guo Zhongjie and others served as inside collaborators, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 宗元及中官方正化不屈死。

translations.literal: Zongyuan and the eunuch Fang Zhenghua refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyuan and the eunuch Fang Zhenghua refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 建泰率曰可、永康出降。

translations.literal: Jiantai led Yueke and Yongkang out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantai led Yueke and Yongkang out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 忠嗣分守東城，城將陷，召女弟適楊千戶者歸，與妻毛、子婦王同處一室，俱以弓弦縊殺之，復登城拒守。

translations.literal: Zhongsi, assigned to defend the eastern wall, when the city was about to fall summoned home his younger sister, married to an officer of the Yang household, and together with his wife Mao and daughter-in-law Wang sat in one room and hanged them all with bowstrings; then he returned to the wall to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongsi was posted to defend the eastern wall; as the city was about to fall he summoned home his younger sister, married to a company commander of the Yang clan, and together with his wife Mao and daughter-in-law Wang gathered them in one room and hanged them all with bowstrings, then returned to the wall to fight on.

sentences.zh: 城破被執，怒詈，奪賊刀殺二賊。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized; cursing furiously, he snatched a rebel sword and killed two rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was seized; cursing in fury, he wrested a rebel sword and killed two of them.

sentences.zh: 賊麕至，剜目劓鼻支解死。

translations.literal: Rebels mobbed him, gouged out his eyes, sliced off his nose, and dismembered him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels mobbed him, gouged out his eyes, cut off his nose, and dismembered him to death.

sentences.zh: 一時武臣死事者，守備則張大同與子之坦力戰死。

translations.literal: Military officials who died in the affair at that time included, among garrison commanders, Zhang Datong and his son Zhitang, who fought fiercely to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Among the military officers who died in the affair at that time, the garrison commander Zhang Datong and his son Zhitang fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 指揮則文運昌、劉洪恩、戴世爵、劉元靖、呂九章、呂一照、李一廣，中軍則楊儒秀，鎮撫則管民治，千戶則楊仁政、李尚忠、紀動、趙世貴、劉本源、侯繼先、張守道，百戶則劉朝卿、劉悅、田守正、王好善、強忠武、王爾祉，把總則郝國忠、申錫，皆殉城死。

translations.literal: Among commanders Wen Yunchang, Liu Hong'en, Dai Shijue, Liu Yuanjing, Lü Jiuzhang, Lü Yizhao, Li Yiguang; among central-army officers Yang Ruxiu; among garrison regulators Guan Minzhi; among company commanders Yang Renzheng, Li Shangzhong, Ji Dong, Zhao Shigui, Liu Benyuan, Hou Jixian, Zhang Shoudao; among platoon leaders Liu Chaoqing, Liu Yue, Tian Shouzheng, Wang Haoshan, Qiang Zhongwu, Wang Erzhi; and among squad leaders Hao Guozhong and Shen Xi—all died with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Among the commanders Wen Yunchang, Liu Hong'en, Dai Shijue, Liu Yuanjing, Lü Jiuzhang, Lü Yizhao, and Li Yiguang; the central-army officer Yang Ruxiu; the garrison regulator Guan Minzhi; the company commanders Yang Renzheng, Li Shangzhong, Ji Dong, Zhao Shigui, Liu Benyuan, Hou Jixian, and Zhang Shoudao; the platoon leaders Liu Chaoqing, Liu Yue, Tian Shouzheng, Wang Haoshan, Qiang Zhongwu, and Wang Erzhi; and the squad leaders Hao Guozhong and Shen Xi—all died with the city.

sentences.zh: 有呂應蛟者，保定右衛人，歷官密雲副總兵，謝事歸。

translations.literal: There was one Lü Yingjiao, a native of the Baoding Right Garrison, who had served as deputy regional commander at Miyun and retired home.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Lü Yingjiao from the Baoding Right Garrison who had served as deputy regional commander at Miyun and then retired home.

sentences.zh: 賊至，總監正化知其能，延與共守，晝夜戮力。

translations.literal: When the rebels came, Grand Director Zhenghua knew his ability and invited him to defend together, striving day and night.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, Grand Director Zhenghua knew his ability and invited him to join the defense; they strove together day and night.

sentences.zh: 城破，短兵鬥殺十余賊而死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he fought at close quarters and killed more than ten rebels before dying.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he fought at close quarters, killed more than ten rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 張羅俊，字元美，清苑人。

translations.literal: Zhang Luojun, styled Yuanmei, was a native of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Luojun, styled Yuanmei, came from Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 父純臣，由武進士歷官署參將、神機營左副將。

translations.literal: His father Chunchen, through the military jinshi route, served as acting regional vice commander and left deputy commander of the Divine Engine Corps.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chunchen, a military jinshi, rose to acting regional vice commander and left deputy commander of the Divine Engine Corps.

sentences.zh: 生六子：羅俊、羅彥、羅士、羅善、羅喆、羅輔。

translations.literal: He fathered six sons: Luojun, Luoyan, Luoshi, Luoshan, Luozhe, and Luofu.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Luojun, Luoyan, Luoshi, Luoshan, Luozhe, and Luofu.

sentences.zh: 羅俊娶瞽女，終身不置妾。

translations.literal: Luojun married a blind woman and never took a concubine in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun married a blind woman and never took a concubine all his life.

sentences.zh: 羅彥，字仲美，舉崇禎二年進士。

translations.literal: Luoyan, styled Zhongmei, passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan, styled Zhongmei, earned his jinshi in the second year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部文選郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted through the ranks to director of the Personnel Selection Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to director of the Personnel Selection Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌數借封疆事引用匪人，羅彥多駁正。

translations.literal: Yang Sichang repeatedly used frontier affairs to bring in unworthy men; Luoyan often refuted and corrected him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang repeatedly used frontier appointments to advance unworthy men, and Luoyan often pushed back against him.

sentences.zh: 帝疑吏部行私，廠卒常充庭，曹郎多罹譴者，羅彥獨無所染。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the Ministry of Personnel of favoritism; eunuch agents often filled the courtyard, and many bureau officials suffered punishment—Luoyan alone was unstained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected the Ministry of Personnel of corruption; eunuch agents thronged the courtyard and many bureau officials were punished, yet Luoyan alone remained untainted.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷光祿少卿，被誣落職歸。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then was slandered, dismissed, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but was slandered, stripped of office, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 羅俊以十六年秋舉進士，羅輔亦以是年舉武進士。

translations.literal: Luojun passed the metropolitan examination in the autumn of the sixteenth year; Luofu also passed the military jinshi examination that year.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun earned his civil jinshi in the autumn of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, and Luofu passed the military jinshi examination the same year.

sentences.zh: 而羅彥少從父塞上，習兵事。

translations.literal: Luoyan in his youth followed his father to the frontier and learned military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan had followed his father to the frontier in his youth and learned the art of war.

sentences.zh: 初官行人，奉使旋裏，鄉郡三被兵，佐當事守禦，三著功。

translations.literal: His first post was courier; returning home on a mission, his home district suffered three invasions, and he assisted the authorities in defense, earning merit three times.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as a courier; on returning home from a mission he found his district invaded three times, and each time he helped the authorities defend it with distinction.

sentences.zh: 給事中時敏奉使過其地，夜半欲入城，羅彥不許。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Shi Min, on a mission passing through the area, wished to enter the city at midnight; Luoyan would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Shi Min, traveling through on official business, wanted to enter the city at midnight; Luoyan refused.

sentences.zh: 敏劾其擅司鎖鑰，羅彥疏辯，帝不問。

translations.literal: Min impeached him for usurping control of the locks and keys; Luoyan memorialized in defense, and the emperor took no action.
translations.idiomatic: Min impeached him for seizing control of the gate keys; Luoyan submitted a memorial in his own defense, and the emperor let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，賊逼京師，眾議守禦。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year rebels pressed on the capital, and all discussed defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year, as rebels closed on the capital, everyone debated how to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 羅彥兄弟與同知邵宗元等歃血盟，誓死守。

translations.literal: The Luoyan brothers and Vice Prefect Shao Zongyuan and others swore a blood oath to die defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Luoyan brothers joined Vice Prefect Shao Zongyuan and others in a blood oath, vowing to hold the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 總兵官馬岱謁羅彥曰：「賊分兩道，一出固關，一趨河間。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ma Dai called on Luoyan and said: "The rebels are split in two columns—one out through Guyuan Pass, one heading for Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ma Dai came to Luoyan and said, "The rebels are advancing in two columns—one through Guyuan Pass, one toward Hejian.

sentences.zh: 吾當出屯蠡縣扼其沖，先殺妻子而後往，其城守悉屬公。」

translations.literal: I shall go out to encamp at Li County and block their thrust, first killing my wife and children and then departing; the entire defense of the city is entrusted to you.
translations.idiomatic: I will march out to Li County to block their advance—I will kill my wife and children first, then go—and leave the whole defense of the city to you.

sentences.zh: 羅彥曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: Luoyan said: "Agreed."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan said, "Very well."

sentences.zh: 詰旦，岱果殺妻孥十一人，率師去。

translations.literal: At dawn Dai indeed killed his wife and eleven dependents and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Dai did kill his wife and eleven family members, then led his troops away.

sentences.zh: 羅彥等糾鄉兵二千分陴守。

translations.literal: Luoyan and the others mustered two thousand local militia and divided them along the parapets to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan and the others raised two thousand local militia and posted them along the walls.

sentences.zh: 羅俊守東城，羅彥西北，羅輔為遊兵。

translations.literal: Luojun defended the eastern wall, Luoyan the northwest, and Luofu served as mobile reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun held the eastern wall, Luoyan the northwest, and Luofu commanded the mobile reserve.

sentences.zh: 公廩不足，出私財佐之。

translations.literal: Public granaries were insufficient, so they contributed private wealth to supplement them.
translations.idiomatic: When public stores ran short, they spent their own money to make up the deficit.

sentences.zh: 賊遣騎呼降，羅俊顧其下曰：「欲降者，取我首去。」

translations.literal: Rebels sent horsemen to call for surrender; Luojun turned to his men and said: "Whoever wishes to surrender may take my head.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel riders called for surrender; Luojun turned to his men and said, "If anyone wants to surrender, take my head first.

sentences.zh: 後衛指揮劉忠嗣挺劍曰：「有不從張氏兄弟死守者，齒此劍。」

translations.literal: Rear Garrison Commander Liu Zhongsi drew his sword and said: "Whoever will not follow the Zhang brothers in dying to defend the city—meet this sword."
translations.idiomatic: Rear Garrison Commander Liu Zhongsi drew his sword and cried, "Whoever will not stand with the Zhang brothers and die defending this city—let this sword find him."

sentences.zh: 怒目，發上指。

translations.literal: His eyes blazed with rage, hair standing on end.
translations.idiomatic: His eyes blazed, every hair on end with fury.

sentences.zh: 聞者鹹憤厲，守益堅，賊為引卻。

translations.literal: All who heard were stirred to fierce resolve; the defense grew firmer still, and the rebels drew back.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard were roused to fury; the defense stiffened, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 已，聞京師變，眾皆哭，北向拜，又羅拜相盟誓。

translations.literal: Soon they heard of the catastrophe at the capital; all wept, bowed toward the north, and bowed to one another again in renewed oath.
translations.idiomatic: Before long came word of the capital's fall; everyone wept, bowed toward the north, and bowed to one another again to renew their oath.

sentences.zh: 而賊攻益急，城中多異議。

translations.literal: But rebel attacks grew fiercer, and dissent spread within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel attacks grew fiercer still, and dissent multiplied inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 羅彥謂宗元曰：「小民無知，非鼓以大義，氣不壯。」

translations.literal: Luoyan said to Zongyuan: "The common people are ignorant; unless roused by great principle, their spirit will not be strong.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan told Zongyuan, "The common people do not understand—unless we stir them with a great cause, their courage will fail.

sentences.zh: 乃下令人綴崇禎錢一枚於項，以示戴主意。

translations.literal: He then ordered each person to wear a Chongzhen coin on a cord about the neck, to show loyalty to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered everyone to wear a Chongzhen coin on a cord around the neck as a sign of loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 賊謂羅彥主謀，呼其名大詬，且射書說降，羅彥不顧。

translations.literal: The rebels said Luoyan was the chief plotter, shouted his name in great abuse, and shot in letters urging surrender; Luoyan paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels named Luoyan as the ringleader, cursed him by name, and shot in letters urging surrender; he ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 賊死傷多，攻愈力。

translations.literal: Rebel dead and wounded were many, yet their attacks grew only more violent.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebel casualties mounted, their assaults grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 李建泰親軍為內應，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Li Jiantai's personal troops served as inside collaborators, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiantai's personal troops turned traitor within the walls, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 羅俊猶持刀砍賊，刀脫，兩手抱賊嚙其耳，血淋漓口吻間。

translations.literal: Luojun still hacked at rebels with a blade; when the blade slipped from his hand he seized a rebel with both arms and bit his ear, blood streaming from his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun still hacked at the rebels until his blade slipped; then he seized a rebel in both arms and bit off his ear, blood streaming from his mouth.

sentences.zh: 賊至益眾，大呼「我進士張羅俊也」，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Rebels closed in ever thicker; he cried aloud "I am Zhang Luojun the jinshi!" and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: More rebels closed in; he shouted, "I am Zhang Luojun the jinshi!" and was slain.

sentences.zh: 羅彥見賊入，急還家，大書官階、姓名於壁，投繯死；

translations.literal: Luoyan saw the rebels enter, hurried home, wrote his rank and name large on the wall, and hanged himself;
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan saw the rebels enter, rushed home, wrote his rank and name large on the wall, and hanged himself;

sentences.zh: 子晉與羅俊子伸並赴井死。

translations.literal: his son Jin and Luojun's son Shen both threw themselves into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: his son Jin and Luojun's son Shen threw themselves into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 羅善，字舜卿，為諸生，佐兩兄守城。

translations.literal: Luoshan, styled Shunqing, was a student and assisted his two elder brothers in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Luoshan, styled Shunqing, was a licentiate who helped his two elder brothers hold the city.

sentences.zh: 城將陷，兩兄戒勿死，羅善曰：「有死節之臣，不可無死節之士。」

translations.literal: As the city was about to fall his brothers warned him not to die; Luoshan said: "Where there are officials who die for principle, there must also be scholars who die for principle.
translations.idiomatic: As the city was about to fall his brothers told him not to die; Luoshan said, "If there are officials who die for principle, there must be scholars who die for principle too.

sentences.zh: 妻高攜三女投井死，羅善亦投他井死。

translations.literal: His wife Gao took their three daughters into a well and died; Luoshan also threw himself into another well and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Gao took their three daughters into a well; Luoshan threw himself into another well.

sentences.zh: 羅輔多力善射，晝夜乘城，射必殺賊。

translations.literal: Luofu was strong and skilled in archery; day and night he manned the wall, and every shot killed a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Luofu was powerfully built and a fine archer; day and night on the wall, every arrow he loosed killed a rebel.

sentences.zh: 城破，與羅俊奪圍走，羅俊不可，羅輔連射殺數人，矢盡，持短兵殺數人乃死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he tried to break out with Luojun, but Luojun would not flee; Luofu shot and killed several in succession, and when his arrows were spent he took up a short weapon, killed several more, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he tried to break out with Luojun, but Luojun refused to flee; Luofu shot several rebels dead in succession, and when his arrows were gone he took up a short weapon, killed several more, and died.

sentences.zh: 張氏兄弟六人，羅士早卒，其妻高守節十七年，至是自經死。

translations.literal: Of the six Zhang brothers, Luoshi had died early; his wife Gao had preserved her chastity for seventeen years and now hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Of the six Zhang brothers, Luoshi had died young; his widow Gao had kept her chastity for seventeen years and now hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 惟羅喆從水門走免，其妻王亦縊死。

translations.literal: Only Luozhe escaped through the water gate; his wife Wang also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Only Luozhe escaped through the water gate; his wife Wang hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 羅俊伯母李罵賊死。

translations.literal: Luojun's aunt by marriage, Lady Li, cursed the rebels and died.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun's aunt by marriage, Lady Li, cursed the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 羅彥妻趙、二妾宋、錢及晉妻師，當圍急時，並坐井傍以待。

translations.literal: Luoyan's wife Zhao, his two concubines Song and Qian, and Jin's wife Shi, when the siege grew desperate, all sat by the well waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyan's wife Zhao, his concubines Song and Qian, and Jin's wife Shi all sat by the well waiting as the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 賊入，皆先羅彥投井死，獨趙不沈，家人出之。

translations.literal: When the rebels entered they all threw themselves into the well before Luoyan; only Zhao did not sink, and the family pulled her out.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered they threw themselves into the well ahead of Luoyan; only Zhao did not drown, and the family pulled her out.

sentences.zh: 羅輔妻白在母家，聞變欲死，侍者止之，紿以汲井，推幼女先入，已從之。

translations.literal: Luofu's wife Bai was at her mother's home; hearing the disaster she wished to die, but attendants stopped her; pretending to draw water at the well she pushed her young daughter in first, then followed.
translations.idiomatic: Luofu's wife Bai was at her mother's house; when she heard the news she wanted to die, but servants stopped her; pretending to draw water at the well she pushed her little daughter in first, then followed.

sentences.zh: 羅俊再從子震妻徐，巽妻劉，亦投井死，一門死者凡二十三人。

translations.literal: Luojun's grandnephew Zhen's wife Xu and Xun's wife Liu also threw themselves into wells and died; deaths in the household totaled twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Luojun's grandnephews Zhen's wife Xu and Xun's wife Liu also threw themselves into wells; twenty-three members of the household died in all.

sentences.zh: 金毓峒，字稚鶴，保定衛人。

translations.literal: Jin Yutong, styled Zhihe, was a native of the Baoding Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Yutong, styled Zhihe, came from the Baoding Garrison.

sentences.zh: 父銓，戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Quan was a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan had been a vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 毓峒舉崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: Yutong passed the metropolitan examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yutong earned his jinshi in the seventh year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 十四年面陳漕務，稱旨，授御史。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he presented grain-transport affairs to the emperor in person, pleased him, and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he spoke to the emperor in person on grain transport, pleased him, and was made a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏論兵部尚書陳新甲庸才誤國，戶部尚書李待問積病妨賢。

translations.literal: In a memorial he argued that Minister of War Chen Xinjia was a mediocrity who harmed the state, and Minister of Revenue Li Daiwen's chronic illness obstructed worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he charged that Minister of War Chen Xinjia was a mediocrity ruining the state and that Minister of Revenue Li Daiwen's chronic illness kept worthy men from office.

sentences.zh: 又請渙發德音，自十五年始，蠲除繁苛，與海內更新。

translations.literal: He also asked that benevolent edicts be promulgated from the fifteenth year onward, abolishing harsh exactions and renewing the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that from the fifteenth year onward the throne issue benevolent edicts, lift harsh levies, and give the empire a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 因言復社一案，其人盡縫掖，不可以一夫私怨開禍端。

translations.literal: He spoke further on the Fushe case, saying its members were all gowned scholars and that one man's private grudge must not open the door to calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On the Fushe case he argued that its members were all scholars in official dress and that one man's private vendetta must not be allowed to unleash disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝多采納。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted much of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted much of what he proposed.

sentences.zh: 明年出按陜西。

translations.literal: The next year he went out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 孫傳庭治兵關中，吏民苦征繕，日夜望出關，天子亦屢詔督趣。

translations.literal: Sun Chuanting was training troops in the Guanzhong region; officials and people suffered under levies and construction, day and night longing for him to march out of the passes, while the Son of Heaven also repeatedly issued edicts urging him on.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chuanting was drilling troops in Guanzhong; officials and commoners groaned under levies and labor, longing day and night for him to march east, while the emperor repeatedly ordered him forward.

sentences.zh: 毓峒獨謂將驕卒悍，未可輕戰，抗疏爭。

translations.literal: Yutong alone said the generals were arrogant and the troops fierce, that battle must not be lightly joined, and memorialized in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Yutong alone argued that the generals were arrogant and the troops unruly, that battle must not be lightly risked, and submitted a memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，師果敗。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this; the army was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen, and the army was indeed destroyed.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，期滿得代，甫出境，而賊入關。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixteenth year his term ended and he was relieved; he had barely left the border when rebels entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixteenth year his term ended; he had barely crossed the border when rebels poured through the passes.

sentences.zh: 復還至朝邑，核上將吏功罪而後行。

translations.literal: He returned to Chaoyi, assessed the merits and faults of generals and officials, and only then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to Chaoyi, reviewed the merits and faults of the officers, and only then moved on.

sentences.zh: 明年三月召對，命監李建泰軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year he was summoned for audience and ordered to supervise Li Jiantai's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he was called to audience and ordered to oversee Li Jiantai's army.

sentences.zh: 馳赴山西，抵保定，賊騎已逼，遂偕邵宗元等共守。

translations.literal: He raced to Shanxi, reached Baoding, found rebel cavalry already pressing close, and joined Shao Zongyuan and others in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: He raced toward Shanxi, reached Baoding to find rebel cavalry already at the gates, and joined Shao Zongyuan and others in holding the city.

sentences.zh: 毓峒分守西城，散家貲千余金犒士，其妻王亦出簪珥佐之。

translations.literal: Yutong was assigned the western wall, distributed more than a thousand taels of his family wealth to reward the troops, and his wife Wang also contributed her hairpins and earrings.
translations.idiomatic: Yutong took the western wall, gave more than a thousand taels of family silver to reward the troops, and his wife Wang added her jewelry.

sentences.zh: 京師變聞，賊射書說降，眾頗懈。

translations.literal: When word came of the capital's fall, rebels shot in letters urging surrender and morale slackened.
translations.idiomatic: When news came of the capital's fall, rebels shot in letters urging surrender and spirits flagged.

sentences.zh: 毓峒厲聲曰：「正當為君父復仇，敢異議者斬！」

translations.literal: Yutong said in a stern voice: "This is the time to avenge our lord and father—whoever dares dissent, behead him!
translations.idiomatic: Yutong cried in a harsh voice, "Now is the time to avenge our sovereign—whoever dares speak otherwise, off with his head!

sentences.zh: 懸銀牌，令擊賊者自取。

translations.literal: He hung up silver tokens and let whoever struck down a rebel take one for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He hung out silver tokens for anyone who killed a rebel to claim.

sentences.zh: 眾爭奮，斃賊多。

translations.literal: All strove fiercely and many rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Men fought with renewed fury and many rebels fell.

sentences.zh: 城陷，一賊挽毓峒往謁其帥，且罵且行，遇井。

translations.literal: When the city fell a rebel dragged Yutong to see their commander, cursing as they went; they came upon a well.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell a rebel dragged Yutong off to see their commander, cursing all the way; they passed a well.

sentences.zh: 推賊仆地，自墮井死。

translations.literal: He shoved the rebel to the ground and threw himself into the well to die.
translations.idiomatic: He threw the rebel down and hurled himself into the well.

sentences.zh: 妻聞，即自經。

translations.literal: When his wife heard, she immediately hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife heard and at once hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 其從子振孫有勇力，以武舉佐守城。

translations.literal: His nephew Zhensun was brave and strong and, a military graduate, assisted in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhensun was strong and brave; a military graduate, he helped defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊至，眾皆散，獨立城上，大呼曰：「我金振孫，前日殺數賊魁者，我也。」

translations.literal: When the rebels came all scattered; he alone stood on the wall and shouted: "I am Jin Zhensun—the one who killed several rebel chiefs the other day—that is me.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came everyone fled; he alone stood on the wall and shouted, "I am Jin Zhensun—the one who killed your chiefs the other day!

sentences.zh: 群賊支解之。

translations.literal: The rebel mob dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels mobbed him and cut him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 振孫兄肖孫、子婦陳與侍兒桂春，亦投井死。

translations.literal: Zhensun's elder brother Xiaosun, his daughter-in-law Chen, and the maid Guichun also threw themselves into wells and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhensun's brother Xiaosun, his daughter-in-law Chen, and the maid Guichun also threw themselves into wells.

sentences.zh: 肖孫匿毓峒二子，為賊搒掠無完膚，終不言，二孤獲免。

translations.literal: Xiaosun hid Yutong's two sons; beaten by rebels until no inch of skin was whole, he still would not speak, and the two orphans were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosun hid Yutong's two sons; the rebels beat him until his body was one wound, yet he never spoke, and the two boys were saved.

sentences.zh: 同時守城殉難者，邠州知州韓東明、武進士陳國政赴井死。

translations.literal: Among those who died defending the city at the same time, Binzhou Prefect Han Dongming and military graduate Chen Guozheng threw themselves into wells.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died in the defense included Binzhou Prefect Han Dongming and military graduate Chen Guozheng, who threw themselves into wells.

sentences.zh: 平涼通判張維綱，舉人張爾翚、孫從範，不屈死。

translations.literal: Pingliang Vice Magistrate Zhang Weigang and juren Zhang Erchong and Sun Congfan refused to submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang Vice Magistrate Zhang Weigang and the juren Zhang Erchong and Sun Congfan refused to yield and died.

sentences.zh: 舉人高經負母避難，遇賊求釋母，母獲釋而經被執，乘間赴水死。

translations.literal: The juren Gao Jing carried his mother to escape; encountering rebels he begged them to release his mother; she was released but he was seized, and seizing an opening he threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The juren Gao Jing fled carrying his mother on his back; when they met rebels he begged them to free her; she was released but he was seized, and he found a moment to throw himself into the water.

sentences.zh: 貢生郭鳴世寢疾，聞城陷，整衣端坐。

translations.literal: The tribute student Guo Mingshi lay ill in bed; hearing the city had fallen he straightened his garments and sat upright.
translations.idiomatic: The tribute student Guo Mingshi lay sick in bed; when he heard the city had fallen he straightened his robes and sat upright.

sentences.zh: 賊至，持棒奮擊而死。

translations.literal: When rebels came he seized a club and struck fiercely until he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came he seized a club and fought until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 諸生王之珽，先城陷一日，置酒會家人，飲達旦。

translations.literal: The student Wang Zhi, one day before the city fell, set out wine for his family and drank until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The licentiate Wang Zhi, a day before the city fell, set out wine for his family and drank until dawn.

sentences.zh: 城破，偕妻齊及三子、二女入井死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he entered a well with his wife Qi, three sons, and two daughters and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he went into a well with his wife Qi, three sons, and two daughters.

sentences.zh: 諸生韓楓、何一中、杜日芳、王法等二十九人，布衣劉宗向、田仰名、劉自重等二十人，或自經，或溺，或受刃，皆不屈死。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine students including Han Feng, He Yizhong, Du Rifang, and Wang Fa, and twenty commoners including Liu Zongxiang, Tian Yangming, and Liu Zizhong—some hanged themselves, some drowned, some met the blade—all died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine licentiates including Han Feng, He Yizhong, Du Rifang, and Wang Fa, and twenty commoners including Liu Zongxiang, Tian Yangming, and Liu Zizhong—by hanging, drowning, or the blade—all died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 婦人盡節者一百十五人。

translations.literal: Women who preserved their chastity numbered one hundred fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred fifteen women died preserving their chastity.

sentences.zh: 他若都給事中尹洗、舉人劉會昌、貢生王聯芳，以城陷次日為賊收獲，亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Others such as Chief Supervising Secretary Yin Xi, juren Liu Huichang, and tribute student Wang Lianfang, seized by rebels the day after the city fell, also died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Others such as Chief Supervising Secretary Yin Xi, the juren Liu Huichang, and tribute student Wang Lianfang, captured the day after the fall, also refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 賊揭其首於竿，書曰：「據城抗節，惡官逆子。」

translations.literal: Rebels displayed their heads on poles with the inscription: "Officials and rebellious sons who held the city and resisted to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels spiked their heads on poles with the label, "Wicked officials and rebellious sons who held the city and resisted.

sentences.zh: 見者飲泣。

translations.literal: Those who saw wept as they swallowed their tears.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw it wept.

sentences.zh: 湯文瓊，字兆鰲，石埭人。

translations.literal: Tang Wenqiong, styled Zhaoo, was a native of Shidi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Wenqiong, styled Zhaoo, came from Shidi.

sentences.zh: 授徒京師，見國事日非，數獻策闕下，不報。

translations.literal: He taught students in the capital; seeing state affairs daily worsen, he repeatedly submitted strategies below the palace gates without response.
translations.idiomatic: He taught in the capital; as affairs worsened day by day he repeatedly submitted plans at the palace gate, but none was answered.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，慨然語其友曰：「吾雖布衣，獨非大明臣子耶？

translations.literal: When the capital fell he said feelingly to his friends: "Though I am but a commoner, am I not still a subject of the Great Ming?
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he said to his friends, "I may be only a commoner, but am I not still a subject of the Great Ming?

sentences.zh: 安忍見賊弒君篡國。」

translations.literal: How can I bear to see rebels murder our lord and usurp the realm.
translations.idiomatic: How can I bear to watch rebels murder our sovereign and steal the realm?

sentences.zh: 乃書其衣衿曰：「位非文丞相之位，心存文丞相之心。」

translations.literal: He then wrote on his collar: "My station is not Chancellor Wen's station, but my heart holds Chancellor Wen's heart."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on his collar, "My rank is not Chancellor Wen's rank, but my heart holds Chancellor Wen's heart."

sentences.zh: 投繯而卒。

translations.literal: He hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: He hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 福王時，給事中熊汝霖上疏曰：「北都之變，臣傳詢南來者，確知魏藻德為報名入朝之首，梁兆陽、楊觀光、何瑞徵為從逆獻謀之首，其他皆稽首賊庭，乞憐恐後。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, Supervising Secretary Xiong Rulin memorialized: "At the catastrophe of the northern capital, this subject questioned those who came south and learned for certain that Wei Zaode was foremost in registering to attend court, that Liang Zhaoyang, Yang Guanguang, and He Ruizheng were foremost in following the rebels and offering counsel, while the rest all kowtowed in the rebel court, begging mercy in fear of being left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, Supervising Secretary Xiong Rulin wrote, "After the fall of the northern capital I questioned those who fled south and learned for certain that Wei Zaode was first to register for audience with the rebels, that Liang Zhaoyang, Yang Guanguang, and He Ruizheng were first to follow them and offer counsel, while the rest all kowtowed in the rebel court, begging for mercy lest they be left behind.

sentences.zh: 而文瓊以閭閻匹夫，乃能抗誌捐生，爭光日月。

translations.literal: Yet Wenqiong, a common man of the lanes, was able to hold fast his will and give his life, vying in glory with sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wenqiong, a common man from the streets, held firm to his purpose and gave his life, outshining the sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 賊聞其衣帶中語，以責陳演，即斬演於市。

translations.literal: Rebels heard the words in his belt and clothing and used them to reproach Chen Yan, immediately executing Yan in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels read what he had written on his collar they used it to condemn Chen Yan and executed him in the marketplace on the spot.

sentences.zh: 文瓊布衣死節，賊猶重之，不亟表章，何以慰忠魂，勵臣節。」

translations.literal: Wenqiong died for principle as a commoner, yet even rebels respected him; if we do not promptly honor him, how shall we comfort loyal souls and encourage officials' integrity?
translations.idiomatic: Wenqiong died for principle though only a commoner, and even the rebels respected him; if we do not honor him at once, how can we comfort loyal souls and stir officials to integrity?

sentences.zh: 乃贈中書舍人，祀旌忠祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made a Secretariat drafter and enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a Secretariat drafter and enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 時都城以布衣盡節者，又有範箴聽、楊鉉、李夢禧、張世禧輩。

translations.literal: At that time among commoners in the capital who died for principle were also Fan Zhenting, Yang Xuan, Li Mengxi, Zhang Shixi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time other commoners in the capital who died for principle included Fan Zhenting, Yang Xuan, Li Mengxi, Zhang Shixi, and others.

sentences.zh: 福王建國，喪亂益甚，且見聞不詳，未盡表章。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fu established his state, mourning and chaos grew worse still, and because reports were incomplete, not all were honored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu established his court, mourning and chaos only deepened, and because records were incomplete, not all were properly honored.

sentences.zh: 箴聽，端方有義行。

translations.literal: Zhenting was upright in bearing and possessed righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenting was upright in character and known for righteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍講學都下，受業其門。

translations.literal: When Gao Panlong lectured in the capital, he studied under his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Panlong lectured in the capital, he became a student in his school.

sentences.zh: 魏國公徐允禎延為館賓，數進規諫。

translations.literal: Duke of Wei Xu Yunzhen retained him as a household guest, and he repeatedly offered remonstrance and counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei, Xu Yunzhen, took him on as a household guest, and he often remonstrated and offered counsel.

sentences.zh: 允禎或倨見他客，箴聽至，輒斂容。

translations.literal: Yunzhen sometimes received other guests haughtily; when Zhenting arrived, he would always compose his demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhen sometimes received other guests with arrogance, but whenever Zhenting appeared he would at once compose himself.

sentences.zh: 賊入，置一棺，偃臥其上，絕食七日死。

translations.literal: When the rebels entered, he placed a coffin, lay stretched upon it, and starved himself for seven days until he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered the city, he had a coffin set out, lay down upon it, and starved himself for seven days until he died.

sentences.zh: 鉉，善寫真。

translations.literal: Xuan was skilled at true-to-life painting.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was skilled at portraiture.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，攜二子赴井死。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, he took his two sons into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, he took his two sons into a well and perished with them.

sentences.zh: 夢禧，負誌節，與妻杜、二子、二女、一婢俱縊死。

translations.literal: Mengxi possessed resolute principle; he, his wife Du, his two sons, two daughters, and one maid all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxi was a man of resolute principle; he, his wife Du, his two sons, two daughters, and one maidservant all hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 世禧，儒士也，亦與二子懋賞、懋官俱縊死。

translations.literal: Shixi was a Confucian scholar; he too hanged himself together with his two sons Maoshang and Maoguan.
translations.idiomatic: Shixi was a scholar; he too hanged himself together with his sons Maoshang and Maoguan.

sentences.zh: 又有周姓者，悲憤槌胸，嘔血數升而死。

translations.literal: There was also a man surnamed Zhou who, in grief and fury, beat his chest, vomited several sheng of blood, and died.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a man surnamed Zhou who, overcome with grief and rage, beat his chest, vomited several sheng of blood, and died.

sentences.zh: 而柏鄉人郝奇遇，居京師，聞變，謂妻曰：「我欲死難，汝能之乎？」

translations.literal: Meanwhile Hao Qiyu of Baixiang, living in the capital, upon hearing of the catastrophe said to his wife: "I wish to die in the nation's cause—can you do likewise?
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Hao Qiyu of Baixiang, who lived in the capital, heard the news and asked his wife, "I mean to die for the dynasty—can you do the same?

sentences.zh: 妻曰：「能。」

translations.literal: His wife said: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: His wife said, "I can."

sentences.zh: 遂先死。

translations.literal: She then died first.
translations.idiomatic: She died first.

sentences.zh: 奇遇瘞畢，服藥死。

translations.literal: After Qiyu had buried her, he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiyu had buried her, he took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 許琰，字玉仲，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Yan, styled Yuzhong, was a man of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan, styled Yuzhong, was from Wu County.

sentences.zh: 幼有至性，嘗刲臂療父疾。

translations.literal: From childhood he possessed utmost filial nature; once he cut his arm to treat his father's illness.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was deeply filial; once he cut flesh from his arm to treat his father's illness.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，磊落不羈。

translations.literal: As a student he was open and bold, unrestrained by convention.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate he was open-hearted and unconstrained by convention.

sentences.zh: 聞京師陷，帝殉社稷，大慟，誓欲舉義兵討賊。

translations.literal: When he heard the capital had fallen and the emperor had died for the altars of state, he was deeply stricken and vowed to raise righteous troops to punish the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the capital had fallen and the emperor had died for the realm, he was stricken with grief and vowed to raise righteous troops against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 走告裏薦紳，皆不應。

translations.literal: He ran to tell the gentry of his district, but none responded.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the local gentry to rally them, but none answered his call.

sentences.zh: 端午日過友人，出酒飲之，琰擲杯大詬曰：「今何日，我輩讀聖賢書，尚縱酒如平日耶！」

translations.literal: On the Dragon Boat Festival he visited a friend, who brought out wine to drink with him; Yan flung down the cup and cursed loudly: "What day is this! We who have read the sages' books—shall we still drink as on ordinary days!
translations.idiomatic: On the Dragon Boat Festival he visited a friend who offered wine; Yan threw down the cup and cursed, "What day is this! We who have read the books of the sages—shall we still drink as though nothing had happened?

sentences.zh: 拂衣徑去。

translations.literal: He brushed his robes and went straight off.
translations.idiomatic: He shook out his robes and left at once.

sentences.zh: 已，聚哭明倫堂，琰衰杖擗踴，號泣盡哀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they gathered to weep at the Hall of Bright Principle; Yan, in mourning garb and leaning on his staff, beat his breast and stamped his feet, wailing with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they gathered to mourn at the Hall of Bright Principle; Yan, in mourning dress and leaning on his staff, beat his breast and stamped his feet, wailing in full grief.

sentences.zh: 御史謁文廟，猶吉服。

translations.literal: A censor visited the Confucian temple still wearing festive dress.
translations.idiomatic: A censor visited the Confucian temple still dressed in festive garb.

sentences.zh: 琰率諸生責以大義，禦中惶悚謝罪去。

translations.literal: Yan led the students in rebuking him with the great principle; the censor, stricken with fear, apologized and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yan led the students in rebuking him on grounds of principle; the censor, terrified, apologized and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及南都頒監國詔，而哀詔猶未頒。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital issued the regency edict, the mourning edict had still not been promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Capital had already issued the regency edict, yet the mourning edict had not yet been promulgated.

sentences.zh: 琰益憤慟，趨古廟自經，為人所解，乃步至胥門，投於河。

translations.literal: Yan grew ever more indignant and anguished; he hurried to an ancient temple to hang himself, was cut down by others, then walked to Xumen Gate and threw himself into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Yan grew ever more anguished; he rushed to an ancient temple to hang himself, was cut down, then walked to Xumen Gate and threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 潞王舟至，拯之出，詢其故，嗟嘆良久。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Lu's boat arrived, men pulled him out and asked his reason; the prince sighed at length.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu's boat passed, men pulled him out and asked why he had done it; the prince sighed long over his answer.

sentences.zh: 識琰者掖以歸，家人旦夕守，不得死，遂絕粒。

translations.literal: Those who knew Yan supported him home; his family kept watch day and night so he could not die, and so he stopped eating.
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew him helped him home; his family watched him day and night and would not let him die, so he stopped eating altogether.

sentences.zh: 尋聞哀詔至，即庭中稽首號慟，並不復言，以六月三日卒。

translations.literal: Soon he heard the mourning edict had arrived; at once in the courtyard he bowed his head to the ground and wailed in anguish, and spoke no more; on the third day of the sixth month he died.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the mourning edict had arrived, he prostrated himself in the courtyard and wailed in anguish, then said no more; on the third day of the sixth month he died.

sentences.zh: 鄉人私謚曰潛忠先生。

translations.literal: The people of his district privately gave him the posthumous title Master Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsmen privately gave him the posthumous title Master Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 南中贈《五經》博士，祀旌忠祠。

translations.literal: The southern court posthumously made him Erudite of the Five Classics and enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The southern court posthumously made him Erudite of the Five Classics and enshrined him in the Hall of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 是時諸生殉義者，京師則曹肅、藺衛卿、周讜、李汝翼，大同則李若葵，金壇則王明灝，丹陽則王介休，雞澤則殷淵，肥鄉則宋湯齊、郭珩、王拱辰。

translations.literal: At that time among students who died for righteousness, in the capital were Cao Su, Lin Weiqing, Zhou Dan, and Li Ruyi; in Datong, Li Ruokui; in Jintan, Wang Minghao; in Danyang, Wang Jiexiu; in Jize, Yin Yuan; and in Feixiang, Song Tangqi, Guo Heng, and Wang Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time students who died for righteousness included, in the capital, Cao Su, Lin Weiqing, Zhou Dan, and Li Ruyi; in Datong, Li Ruokui; in Jintan, Wang Minghao; in Danyang, Wang Jiexiu; in Jize, Yin Yuan; and in Feixiang, Song Tangqi, Guo Heng, and Wang Gongchen.

sentences.zh: 肅，曾祖子登，仕為甘肅巡撫。

translations.literal: Su's great-grandfather Zideng had served as grand coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Su's great-grandfather Zideng had served as grand coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 賊入，肅與祖母姜、母張、嫂李及弟持敏、妹持順、弟婦鄧並自縊。

translations.literal: When the rebels entered, Su, together with his grandmother Jiang, his mother Zhang, his sister-in-law Li, his younger brothers Chimin and Zhishun, his younger sister Zhishun, and his brother's wife Deng, all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels entered, Su hanged himself together with his grandmother Jiang, his mother Zhang, his sister-in-law Li, his younger brothers Chimin and Zhishun, his younger sister Zhishun, and his brother's wife Deng.

sentences.zh: 衛卿止一幼女，托其友，亦自縊，讜被執，罵賊不屈死。

translations.literal: Weiqing had only one young daughter, whom he entrusted to a friend, then hanged himself; Dan was seized, cursed the rebels, and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Weiqing had only one young daughter, whom he entrusted to a friend before hanging himself; Dan was captured, cursed the rebels, and was killed without yielding.

sentences.zh: 汝翼，布政使本緯子。

translations.literal: Ruyi was the son of Administration Commissioner Li Benwei.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi was the son of Administration Commissioner Li Benwei.

sentences.zh: 亦罵賊，被磔死。

translations.literal: He too cursed the rebels and was dismembered to death.
translations.idiomatic: He too cursed the rebels and was executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 若蔡與親屬九人皆自縊，題曰一門完節。

translations.literal: Ruokui and nine relatives all hanged themselves, inscribing the words: "One household preserved in full integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Ruokui and nine kinsmen all hanged themselves, leaving an inscription that read, "One household preserved in full integrity."

sentences.zh: 明灝聞變，日夕慟哭，家人解慰之。

translations.literal: Minghao, upon hearing of the catastrophe, wept in anguish day and night; his family tried to comfort and restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Minghao wept in anguish day and night when he heard the news; his family tried to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 托故走二十里外，投水死。

translations.literal: On a pretext he went twenty li beyond the city and drowned himself.
translations.idiomatic: On a pretext he went twenty li beyond the city and drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 介休，不食七日死。

translations.literal: Jiexiu starved himself for seven days and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiexiu starved himself for seven days and died.

sentences.zh: 淵，字仲弘。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Zhonghong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Zhonghong.

sentences.zh: 父大白，官監軍副使，為楊嗣昌所殺。

translations.literal: His father Dabai had served as deputy military supervisor and was killed by Yang Sichang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dabai had served as deputy military supervisor and was killed by Yang Sichang.

sentences.zh: 淵負奇氣。

translations.literal: Yuan possessed an extraordinary spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a man of extraordinary spirit.

sentences.zh: 從父兵間，善技擊，嘗欲報父仇。

translations.literal: He followed his father in military camps, was skilled in combat, and once wished to avenge his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed his father through the camps, was skilled in fighting, and had long wished to avenge his father's death.

sentences.zh: 及賊破雞澤，謀起兵恢復。

translations.literal: When rebels took Jize, he plotted to raise troops and recover the territory.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels seized Jize, he plotted to raise troops and recover the district.

sentences.zh: 俄聞京師陷，即同諸生黃祐等悲號發喪，約山中壯士，誅賊所置官。

translations.literal: Soon he heard the capital had fallen; at once, together with the student Huang You and others, he wailed and raised mourning, and joined with stalwart men in the hills in a pact to kill the officials the rebels had installed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard the capital had fallen; at once he joined the student Huang You and others in wailing and raising mourning, and made a pact with stalwart men in the hills to kill the officials the rebels had installed.

sentences.zh: 偽令秦植踉蹌走，乃入城，行哭臨禮，義聲大震。

translations.literal: The puppet magistrate Qin Zhi fled in panic; Yuan then entered the city, performed the walking mourning rites, and righteous fervor shook the region.
translations.idiomatic: The puppet magistrate Qin Zhi fled in panic; Yuan then entered the city, performed the walking mourning rites, and the cry of righteousness shook the whole region.

sentences.zh: 為奸人所乘，被殺，遠近悼之。

translations.literal: Taken advantage of by a villain, he was killed; near and far mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: Betrayed by a villain, he was killed; people near and far mourned him.

sentences.zh: 湯齊、珩、拱辰亦起兵討賊，為賊將張汝行所害。

translations.literal: Tangqi, Heng, and Gongchen also raised troops to punish the rebels and were killed by the rebel general Zhang Ruxing.
translations.idiomatic: Tangqi, Heng, and Gongchen also raised troops against the rebels and were killed by the rebel general Zhang Ruxing.

sentences.zh: 王喬棟，雄縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiaodong was a man of Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiaodong was from Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授朝邑知縣。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate of Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 縣人王之寀為魏忠賢黨所惡，坐以贓，下喬棟嚴征。

translations.literal: Wang Zhicai of the county was hated by the faction of Wei Zhongxian and was charged with corruption; Qiaodong was ordered to levy heavy exactions.
translations.idiomatic: A county man, Wang Zhicai, was hated by Wei Zhongxian's faction and was charged with corruption; Qiaodong was ordered to levy heavy exactions against him.

sentences.zh: 喬棟不忍，封印於庫而去。

translations.literal: Qiaodong could not bear it, sealed the treasury, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaodong could not bear it; he sealed the treasury and resigned.

sentences.zh: 巡撫怒，將劾之。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator was enraged and was about to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator was furious and was about to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 士民擁署號呼，乃止。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners thronged the yamen shouting; only then did the matter stop.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners thronged the yamen in protest, and the impeachment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起順天教授，累遷湖廣參政。

translations.literal: In the early Chongzhen reign he was recalled as professor of Shuntian and was promoted through the ranks to vice commissioner in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chongzhen reign he was recalled as professor of Shuntian and rose through the ranks to vice commissioner in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 楚中大亂，諸道監司多不至，喬棟兼綰數篆。

translations.literal: Great disorder broke out in Chu; many supervising commissioners of the various circuits did not come to their posts, and Qiaodong concurrently held several seals of office.
translations.idiomatic: Great disorder broke out in Huguang; many circuit supervisors failed to take up their posts, and Qiaodong held several offices at once.

sentences.zh: 乙酉夏，李自成據武昌，喬棟時駐興國州。

translations.literal: In the summer of yiyou, Li Zicheng seized Wuchang; Qiaodong was then stationed at Xingguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of yiyou, Li Zicheng seized Wuchang; Qiaodong was then stationed at Xingguo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城為賊陷，自經城樓上。

translations.literal: When the city fell to the rebels, he hanged himself atop the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell to the rebels, he hanged himself on the gate tower.

sentences.zh: 張繼孟，字伯功，扶風人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jimeng, styled Bogong, was a man of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jimeng, styled Bogong, was from Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the final years of the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the final years of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 知濰縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年擢南京御史，未出都，奏籌邊六事，末言己被抑南臺，由錢神世界，公道無權，宜嚴禁饋遺。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he was promoted to censor in Nanjing; before leaving the capital he memorialized on six matters of frontier planning, and at the end said that he himself had been suppressed by assignment to the southern board because in a world ruled by the god of money, public justice had no power, and gift-giving should be strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianqi he was promoted to censor in Nanjing; before leaving the capital he memorialized on six matters of frontier planning, and at the end said he had been relegated to the southern board because in a world ruled by the god of money public justice had no weight, and that gift-giving should be strictly forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帝令實指，繼孟以風聞對，詔詰責之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to name names specifically; Jimeng answered with hearsay, and an edict rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to name names; Jimeng answered with hearsay, and an edict rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 左都御史趙南星言：「今天下進士重而舉貢輕，京官重而外官輕，在北之科道重而南都輕。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Zhao Nanxing said: "Today jinshi are valued while tribute graduates are slighted, capital officials are valued while outer officials are slighted, and among the censorate the northern board is valued while the southern is slighted.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Zhao Nanxing said, "Today jinshi are prized while tribute graduates are slighted, capital officials are prized while provincial officials are slighted, and among the censorate the northern board is prized while the southern is slighted.

sentences.zh: 乞因繼孟言，思偏重之弊。

translations.literal: I beg that in light of Jimeng's words Your Majesty consider the harm of such imbalance.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that in light of Jimeng's words Your Majesty consider the harm of such imbalance.

sentences.zh: 敕下吏部極力挽回，於用人不為無補。」

translations.literal: If an edict were sent down ordering the Ministry of Personnel to make every effort to reverse this, it would not be without benefit to the employment of men.
translations.idiomatic: If an edict were sent ordering the Ministry of Personnel to make every effort to reverse this, it would not be without benefit in the use of men.

sentences.zh: 於是忌者鹹指目繼孟為東林。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who resented him all pointed at Jimeng as one of the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his enemies all pointed to Jimeng as a Donglin man.

sentences.zh: 尋以不建魏忠賢祠，斥為邪黨，削奪歸。

translations.literal: Soon, for refusing to build a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, he was condemned as a wicked partisan, stripped of rank, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for refusing to build a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, he was condemned as a wicked partisan, stripped of rank, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年起故官，上言：

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was restored to office and memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he was restored to office and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 近見冢臣王永光「人言踵至」一疏，語語謬戾。

translations.literal: Recently I saw Grand Secretary Wang Yongguang's memorial "As Talk Keeps Coming," and every word in it is perverse and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Recently I saw Grand Secretary Wang Yongguang's memorial "As Talk Keeps Coming," and every word in it is perverse and wrong.

sentences.zh: 其曰「惠世揚等借題當議」。

translations.literal: It says that "Hui Shiyang and others seized a pretext and ought to be debated."
translations.idiomatic: It says that "Hui Shiyang and others seized a pretext and ought to be debated."

sentences.zh: 夫雲借者，無其事而借名也。

translations.literal: To say one "seizes" is to borrow a name where no matter exists.
translations.idiomatic: To speak of "seizing" is to borrow a name where no matter exists.

sentences.zh: 世揚與楊漣、左光鬥同事同心，但未同死耳。

translations.literal: Shiyang served in the same cause and with the same heart as Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou—only he did not die with them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyang served in the same cause and with the same heart as Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou—only he did not die with them.

sentences.zh: 今楊、左業有定議，世揚方昭揭於天下後世，奈何以借名之，謬一。

translations.literal: Now Yang and Zuo already have settled verdicts, while Shiyang is being made clear to the world and to posterity—how then can one call this borrowing a name? That is the first error.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and Zuo already have settled verdicts, while Shiyang's honor is now clear to the world and to posterity—how then can one call this borrowing a name? That is the first error.

sentences.zh: 又曰「高捷、史褷發奸已驗，特用宜先。」

translations.literal: It also says that "Gao Jie and Shi Shi exposed wrongdoing that has been verified, and their special appointment should come first.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that "Gao Jie and Shi Shi exposed wrongdoing that has been verified, and their special appointment should come first.

sentences.zh: 夫捷、褷之糾劉鴻訓也，為楊維垣等報仇耳。

translations.literal: When Jie and Shi impeached Liu Hongxun, it was only to avenge Yang Weiyuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie and Shi impeached Liu Hongxun, it was merely to avenge Yang Weiyuan and others.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓輔政，止此一事快人意。

translations.literal: In Hongxun's time as chief minister, this alone pleased men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Of Hongxun's conduct as chief minister, this alone pleased men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其後獲罪以納賄，非以捷、褷劾也。

translations.literal: He was later punished for taking bribes, not because Jie and Shi impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later punished for taking bribes, not because Jie and Shi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 今指護奸者為發奸，謬二。

translations.literal: Now to call those who shielded the wicked men who expose wrongdoing is the second error.
translations.idiomatic: To call men who shielded the wicked "exposers of wrongdoing" is the second error.

sentences.zh: 又曰「諸臣所擁戴者，錢謙益、李騰芳、孫慎行。」

translations.literal: It also says that "the officials whom the ministers champion are Qian Qianyi, Li Tengfang, and Sun Shenxing.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that "the officials whom the ministers champion are Qian Qianyi, Li Tengfang, and Sun Shenxing.

sentences.zh: 夫謙益本末，陛下近亦洞然。

translations.literal: As for Qianyi's whole story, Your Majesty has lately seen it clearly.
translations.idiomatic: As for Qianyi's whole story, Your Majesty has lately seen it clearly enough.

sentences.zh: 至騰芳、慎行，天下共推服。

translations.literal: As for Tengfang and Shenxing, the empire together esteems and accepts them.
translations.idiomatic: As for Tengfang and Shenxing, the empire together esteems them.

sentences.zh: 會推之時，永光身主其議。

translations.literal: At the time of the joint recommendation, Yongguang himself presided over the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the joint recommendation, Yongguang himself presided over the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 乃指公論為擁戴，謬三。

translations.literal: Yet he calls public consensus "championing"—that is the third error.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he calls public consensus "championing"—that is the third error.

sentences.zh: 又曰「欲諸臣疏一面網，息天下朋黨之局。」

translations.literal: It also says that "he wishes the ministers' memorial to show one-sided leniency, so as to quiet the empire's factional strife.
translations.idiomatic: It also says that "he wishes the ministers' memorial to show one-sided leniency, so as to quiet the empire's factional strife.

sentences.zh: 信斯言也，則部議漏張文熙等數十人，是為疏網，而陛下嚴核議罪，反開朋黨之局乎？

translations.literal: If this were true, then the ministry's deliberation omitted several dozen men such as Zhang Wenxi—would that be leniency? Yet Your Majesty strictly reviewed and punished them—is that opening factional strife instead?
translations.idiomatic: If that were true, then the ministry's deliberation omitted several dozen men such as Zhang Wenxi—would that be leniency? Yet Your Majesty strictly reviewed and punished them—is that opening factional strife instead?

sentences.zh: 謬四。

translations.literal: That is the fourth error.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth error.

sentences.zh: 且永光先為御史李應升所糾，今又為御史馬孟正、徐尚勛等所論。

translations.literal: Moreover Yongguang was first impeached by Censor Li Yingsheng, and now is again attacked by Censors Ma Mengzheng, Xu Shangxun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Yongguang was first impeached by Censor Li Yingsheng, and is now again attacked by Censors Ma Mengzheng, Xu Shangxun, and others.

sentences.zh: 而推轂永光者先為崔呈秀、徐大化，今則霍維華、楊維垣、張文熙，其賢不肖可知矣。

translations.literal: Those who promoted Yongguang were first Cui Chengxiu and Xu Dahua; now they are Huo Weihua, Yang Weiyuan, and Zhang Wenxi—their worth and baseness may be known from this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who promoted Yongguang were first Cui Chengxiu and Xu Dahua; now they are Huo Weihua, Yang Weiyuan, and Zhang Wenxi—the worth of the man may be known from this.

sentences.zh: 後又劾南京兵部尚書胡應臺貪汙。

translations.literal: Later he again impeached Minister of War Hu Yingtai of Nanjing for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Later he again impeached Nanjing Minister of War Hu Yingtai for corruption.

sentences.zh: 帝並不納。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted none of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted none of it.

sentences.zh: 永光深疾之，出為廣西知府。

translations.literal: Yongguang hated him deeply and had him transferred out as prefect of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang hated him deeply and had him transferred out as prefect of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 土酋普名聲久亂未靖，繼孟設計鴆之，一方遂安。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Pu Mingsheng had long been in rebellion and the region was not yet pacified; Jimeng devised a plan to poison him, and the region was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chief Pu Mingsheng had long been in rebellion and the region was not yet pacified; Jimeng devised a plan to poison him, and the region was then pacified.

sentences.zh: 稍遷浙江鹽運使，忤視鹽內官崔璘，左遷保寧知府。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang; he offended the salt-inspecting eunuch Cui Lin and was demoted to prefect of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to salt transport commissioner of Zhejiang; he offended the salt-inspecting eunuch Cui Lin and was demoted to prefect of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 尋進副使，分巡川西。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice commissioner and assigned to patrol western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to vice commissioner and assigned to patrol western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十七年八月，張獻忠寇成都，與陳其赤、張孔教、鄭安民、方堯相等佐巡撫龍文光協守，城陷被執。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, Zhang Xianzhong raided Chengdu; together with Chen Qichi, Zhang Kongjiao, Zheng Anmin, and Fang Yaoxiang he assisted Grand Coordinator Long Wenguang in the joint defense; the city fell and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, Zhang Xianzhong raided Chengdu; together with Chen Qichi, Zhang Kongjiao, Zheng Anmin, and Fang Yaoxiang he helped Grand Coordinator Long Wenguang defend the city; when it fell he was captured.

sentences.zh: 獻忠僭帝號，欲用諸人備百官。

translations.literal: Xianzhong usurped an imperial title and wished to employ these men to fill the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong declared himself emperor and wished to employ these men to fill the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 繼孟等不為屈，乃被殺，妻賈從之。

translations.literal: Jimeng and the others would not yield; they were then killed, and his wife Jia followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Jimeng and the others would not submit; they were then killed, and his wife Jia died with him.

sentences.zh: 劉士鬥，字瞻甫，南海人。

translations.literal: Liu Shidou, styled Zhanfu, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shidou, styled Zhanfu, came from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 知太倉州，有政聲。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Taicang Prefecture, he won a reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Taicang Prefecture, he earned a reputation for sound governance.

sentences.zh: 忤上官，中許典，謫江西按察司知事，擢成都推官。

translations.literal: He offended his superiors, failed an assessment, was demoted to clerk in the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission, and was then promoted to reviewing secretary at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He offended his superiors, failed an assessment, was demoted to clerk in the Jiangxi Surveillance Commission, and was later promoted to reviewing secretary at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 十六年，御史劉之勃薦為建昌兵備僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Censor Liu Zhibo recommended him as military intendant of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, Censor Liu Zhibo recommended him for appointment as military intendant of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 明年八月，賊將入境，之勃促之行。
